note: Highest single-year total at the time. COVID-19 outbreaks in detention facilities account for multiple deaths. ACLU documented ICE refusing to release medically vulnerable detainees despite risk.

New all-time record for ICE deaths in a single fiscal year. Detention Watch Network counts 31 for calendar year 2025. Advocates attribute to overcrowding, inadequate medical staffing, and rapid detention expansion under Trump second term.

category: Deaths in ICE Custody (Calendar Year 2026, through Aug 4, 2026)
source: NBC News / AP / ICE.gov / HRW / PHR (Aug 2026)
note: At least 24 people have died in ICE custody in calendar 2026 through Aug 4. The June 25, 2026 HRW/PHR 'Dying in Detention' report documented 52 deaths in the 500 days between Trump's Jan 20, 2025 inauguration and June 4, 2026 — a trend-adjusted mortality rate (8.4 per 10,000 detainees) nearly triple the Biden administration's rate; mortality rose 138% while the detained population grew 77%. Two named deaths since that report: Jesús Manuel Arenas-Silva (45, Venezuela), found unresponsive July 13 while being bus-transferred from Irwin County Detention Center (Ocilla, GA) to the Folkston D. Ray James facility — suspected cardiac arrest; his family says ICE denied his medications and had been in custody only 4 days. Priciliano Trejo (29, Mexico) died July 24 at Stewart Detention Center (Lumpkin, GA) after his family says his leukemia went untreated; he was hospitalized, lapsed into a coma, and died roughly three weeks after falling ill. Mexico's government separately documented 17 Mexican nationals dead in ICE custody or operations since Jan 2025 and is filing criminal complaints with U.S. prosecutors. Acting Director Venturella's June 4 memo ending 30-day post-release death reporting remains in effect; DHS has not restored the OIDO oversight office shuttered May 5, 2026. PHR estimates 95% of ICE custody deaths are likely preventable.

category: Mexican Nationals Dead in ICE Custody/Operations (Since Jan 2025)
note: Mexican government identified 17 Mexican nationals who died in connection with U.S. immigration enforcement since Trump's Jan 2025 inauguration: 14 died in ICE custody or at medical facilities they were sent to; 3 died during enforcement operations, including Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a 52-year-old Houston construction worker fatally shot by an ICE officer July 7, 2026. President Claudia Sheinbaum announced Mexico is filing complaints with U.S. state and federal prosecutors requesting criminal investigations and sent cease-and-desist letters to private companies operating the detention centers involved. DHS disputes some individual accounts, including Salgado Araujo's shooting, where three passengers contest the agency's version of events.

source: HRW — Deaths in ICE Custody Report (2018); ICE.gov historical data
note: Human Rights Watch reported approximately 180 deaths in ICE custody between FY2003 and FY2017, averaging roughly 12 per year. Pre-2018 data is less systematic; mandatory 90-day death reviews not required until FY2018 appropriations.

First year of mandatory death review reporting under Congressional requirement. Seven deaths documented; ICE published 90-day reviews as required. Includes Gourgen Mirimanian (Adelanto) and Huy Chi Tran.

Eight deaths in FY2019. Includes Simratpal Singh (Sikh activist detained at Sacramento), whose case drew significant media attention. DHS OIG investigated multiple deaths for medical care deficiencies.

Five deaths in Biden's first fiscal year — reduction from the COVID-era FY2020 high. Still includes preventable deaths from inadequate medical care. ACLU continued litigation over conditions at Adelanto and Stewart facilities.

Spike to 12 deaths in FY2024 under Biden, ahead of detention population growth. Notable deaths include Ousmane Ba (Senegal) whose family alleged medical neglect at Otay Mesa detention center. Congressional investigation requested.

category: Children Separated from Parents (2018 Family Separation Crisis)
source: DHS IG; Ms. L v. ICE Court Record; HHS
note: Over 2,700 children separated from parents under zero tolerance policy (May–June 2018); some estimates reach 4,000+ when accounting for pre-zero-tolerance separations. Hundreds of families not reunified years later. Long-term psychological trauma documented by pediatric and mental health experts.

killed: Multiple (COVID-linked deaths included in FY2020 count)
